Class GTNetRequestBudgetService

java.lang.Object
grafiosch.gtnet.GTNetRequestBudgetService
@Component public class GTNetRequestBudgetService extends Object
Owns the per-peer daily request budget published as GTNet.getDailyRequestLimit(). The budget is charged in both directions and both counters live on the peer's GTNetConfig:
  • inbound — every request another instance sends us raises dailyRequestLimitCount and is refused with GNetCoreMessageCode.GT_NET_DAILY_REQUEST_LIMIT_EXCEEDED_S once our own limit is reached
  • outbound — every request we send raises dailyRequestLimitRemoteCount and is suppressed once the limit that peer published to us is reached, so we back off before the peer has to refuse us
Only messages whose handler reports MessageCategory.REQUEST are charged. Responses are answers to requests that were already charged on the way out, and announcements are one-way notifications. Three request codes are exempt as well, because a peer must never be able to spend itself out of connectivity or recovery: ping, first handshake and token refresh. There is no reset job. Both counters carry the UTC day they belong to in dailyRequestLimitDate, and the charging statement rolls them over when it meets a request of a new day — which stays correct across a restart or a downtime spanning midnight.

  • Method Details

    • chargeIncoming

      public boolean chargeIncoming(GTNet remoteGTNet, GTNet myGTNet, byte messageCode)
      Charges an incoming request of the given remote against the budget this server grants it. On success the freshly stored count is copied back into the in-memory GTNetConfig, so an auto-answer rule comparing dailyCount sees the request it is deciding about rather than the state before it arrived.
      Parameters:
      remoteGTNet - the sender, null for a first handshake from an unknown domain
      myGTNet - the local entry, whose dailyRequestLimit is the budget
      messageCode - the request's message code
      Returns:
      true when the request may be served, false when the remote has used up its allowance for the day

    • chargeOutgoing

      public boolean chargeOutgoing(GTNet targetGTNet, byte messageCode)
      Charges a request this server is about to send against the budget the target published to us.
      Parameters:
      targetGTNet - the remote we want to send to
      messageCode - the request's message code
      Returns:
      true when the request may be sent, false when we have used up what that peer grants us today
